summary: This informational RFC describes strategies for promoting compliance with IETF IPR disclosure rules. Noncompliance can delay or derail specifications, so it discusses ways to encourage disclosure.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC suggests points in the IETF document process when chairs and area directors can remind people to disclose relevant intellectual property. The reminders aim to surface information early, before a group has committed to a technical direction.

subtitle: Suggested checkpoints for reminding IETF contributors about intellectual property disclosures.

tldr.problem: Late or missing intellectual property disclosures can make a working group revisit decisions and delay a specification.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC suggests asking authors and contributors about disclosures at meeting presentations, working-group adoption, Last Call, area-director review, and IETF Last Call.
tldr.outcome: These are reminders, not new enforcement duties or changes to existing disclosure rules. RFC 6702 is updated by RFC 8717.

today: RFC 6702 is an Informational RFC published in August 2012. It is updated by RFC 8717.

sections.title: Why Early Disclosure Matters
sections.content:
Working groups need information about intellectual property rights (IPR) when they consider technical proposals. If a disclosure arrives after a major decision, the group may have to reconsider its choice or change the specification.

The RFC says the disclosure duties already exist in other IETF documents. This document does not modify those rules or create new mandatory duties for area directors, working-group chairs, or secretaries; it suggests ways they can encourage compliance.
sections.plainLanguage: A group can make a better-informed choice when it knows about relevant intellectual property early. This RFC suggests reminders but does not change who is responsible for making disclosures.

sections.title: Checkpoints for Working-Group Documents
sections.content:
Before a draft is presented at a meeting, chairs can ask its authors and listed contributors to confirm that formal disclosures have been filed. If the draft is early, the chair may allow an informal disclosure and record it in the meeting minutes.

Chairs can ask about IPR when considering adoption and again before Working Group Last Call. During area-director review, the document shepherd is asked whether each author confirmed the required disclosures. IETF Last Call messages include links to disclosures associated with the draft, and those links should be preserved if the message is edited.
sections.plainLanguage: Chairs can ask authors and contributors about disclosures at several stages, including before adoption and before a working-group Last Call. Repeating the question can catch new information or earlier oversights.

sections.title: Individual Submissions
sections.content:
Documents handled outside a working group have similar checkpoints. A meeting chair can ask the authors and listed contributors to confirm disclosures before approving a presentation slot. If the proposal is not yet written as a draft, the chair can request an informal disclosure.

An area director considering sponsorship can ask each author and contributor to confirm that disclosures have been submitted. The shepherd write-up and IETF Last Call also provide opportunities to check disclosure information.
sections.plainLanguage: Individual submissions also receive disclosure reminders before they advance. Meeting chairs and area directors can ask authors and contributors directly.

sections.title: Preliminary Disclosures and Limits
sections.content:
An early disclosure may become incomplete as information changes, for example when a patent application later results in a granted patent. The RFC encourages chairs and area directors to ask the IETF Executive Director to contact people who made preliminary disclosures at later milestones.

The conclusion is explicit: chairs and area directors are not expected to enforce IPR rules. They are encouraged to raise the subject at key points. The RFC says these suggested procedures have no direct impact on Internet security.
sections.plainLanguage: An early disclosure may need an update, so the RFC suggests checking again at later stages. Chairs and area directors remind participants; they are not assigned an enforcement role.
